items.readable_text:
Content:
Until now, we have considered limits at individual points:

Content:
> [MATH: \lim\limits_{x \to a} f(x)] is the value that [MATH: f(x)] approaches as [MATH: x] approaches the point [MATH: a.]

Content:
However, the idea of a limit extends beyond individual points. For instance, it might also be the case that [MATH: f(x)] approaches some value as [MATH: x] gets bigger and bigger, growing without bound.

Content:
To illustrate, consider the function [MATH: f(x)=\dfrac{1}{x} + 1] whose graph is shown below.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/b75a6c31450c66be56a6b52cb5ebd2aa]

Content:
On the right side of the graph, we see that as [MATH: x] gets bigger and bigger, [MATH: f(x)] approaches the horizontal asymptote [MATH: y=1.] In other words, as [MATH: x] increases to infinity ([MATH: \infty]), the value of [MATH: f(x)] approaches a limit of [MATH: 1.] We can write this symbolically as

Content:
[MATH: \lim_\limits{x\to \infty } f(x) = 1.]

Content:
Likewise, on the left side of the graph, as [MATH: x] decreases to negative infinity ([MATH: -\infty]), the value of [MATH: f(x)] approaches the same horizontal asymptote [MATH: y=1.] Consequently, we also have that

Content:
[MATH: \lim_\limits{x\to -\infty } f(x) = 1.]

Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
Until now, we have considered limits at individual points:

Content:
> [MATH: \lim\limits_{x \to a} f(x)] is the value that [MATH: f(x)] approaches as [MATH: x] approaches the point [MATH: a.]

Content:
However, the idea of a limit extends beyond individual points. For instance, it might also be the case that [MATH: f(x)] approaches some value as [MATH: x] gets bigger and bigger, growing without bound.

Content:
To illustrate, consider the function [MATH: f(x)=\dfrac{1}{x} + 1] whose graph is shown below.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/b75a6c31450c66be56a6b52cb5ebd2aa]

Content:
On the right side of the graph, we see that as [MATH: x] gets bigger and bigger, [MATH: f(x)] approaches the horizontal asymptote [MATH: y=1.] In other words, as [MATH: x] increases to infinity ([MATH: \infty]), the value of [MATH: f(x)] approaches a limit of [MATH: 1.] We can write this symbolically as

Content:
[MATH: \lim_\limits{x\to \infty } f(x) = 1.]

Content:
Likewise, on the left side of the graph, as [MATH: x] decreases to negative infinity ([MATH: -\infty]), the value of [MATH: f(x)] approaches the same horizontal asymptote [MATH: y=1.] Consequently, we also have that

Content:
[MATH: \lim_\limits{x\to -\infty } f(x) = 1.]
